entry: French actress who has worked in both European and Hollywood productions. She won an Academy Award for playing [[Édith Piaf]] in *La Vie en Rose* (2007), becoming the only actor to win an Academy Award for a French-language performance. She was also nominated for an Academy Award for *Two Days, One Night* (2014) and has acted in English-language films including *Inception* (2010), *Midnight in Paris* (2011) and *Macbeth* (2015). On stage she has played [[Joan of Arc]] in numerous productions of *Joan of Arc at the Stake* in several countries. She has been a spokeswoman for Greenpeace since 2001.

American actress known for comedic and dramatic roles on screen and stage. Born in [[Brooklyn]], New York, she won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her comedic performance in *My Cousin Vinny* (1992). She was nominated in the same category for *In the Bedroom* (2001) and *The Wrestler* (2008). Early roles included the soap opera *As the World Turns* and the [[Sitcom|sitcom]] *A Different World*. She played May Parker in the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] from *Captain America: Civil War* (2016). Her Broadway debut, in *Wait Until Dark* (1998), was opposite [[Quentin Tarantino]].

American business executive and former software engineer. She was the first woman software engineer at [[Google]] and later a long-time executive and spokesperson for the company. As president and chief executive officer of [[Yahoo]] from 2012 to 2017, she pursued acquisitions, including [[Tumblr]], and enforced a return-to-office policy. Yahoo was sold to Verizon in 2017. Mayer graduated from [[Stanford University]] with degrees in symbolic systems and computer science. She later co-founded Sunshine and founded the [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]] company Dazzle AI. In June 2025 she joined the board of [[Starbucks]].

Study of human interaction with and activity at sea. The field often takes a global approach, although national and regional histories remain predominant. Its subjects include fishing, whaling, maritime law, naval history, ship design, shipbuilding, navigation, the history of [[Oceanography|oceanography]], [[Cartography|cartography]] and [[Hydrography|hydrography]], lighthouses, maritime trade and seafaring communities. Inland waterways, especially the [[Great Lakes]] and navigable rivers and canals, are also included. Scholars have divided the field into Traditionalists, who write for other academics, and Utilitarians, who seek to influence policy makers and a wider audience. Recent scholarship has examined the people who used ships and, through the concept of sub-oceanic history, the ocean's interior.

Transport of people or goods via waterways. Maritime transport, also called ocean or waterborne transport, can operate over any distance where navigable oceans, lakes, rivers and canals connect. It has been widely used throughout recorded history because it offers higher capacity than land transport, which is typically more costly per unit of payload. Watercraft are much cheaper than aircraft or road and rail vehicles but are slower over long journeys and depend on adequate [[Port|port]] facilities. According to UNCTAD, maritime transport accounts for roughly 80% of international trade in 2020. Containerization revolutionized the industry from the 1970s. Water transport is highly cost-effective for heavy or bulk cargo, such as coal, [[Coke (fuel)|coke]], [[Ore|ores]] and grains. According to the 2005 CIA World Factbook, there were 30,936 merchant ships of at least 1,000 gross register tons in the world; in 2010 the total was 38,988, an increase of 26%.

French and Russian ballet dancer, pedagogue and choreographer. Born in [[Marseille]], France, he was raised in [[Brussels]] and trained in ballet under his father, Jean-Antoine Petipa. He performed as a principal dancer in [[Bordeaux]], Paris and Madrid before joining the St. Petersburg Imperial Theatres in 1847. From 1871 until 1903 he was ballet master and principal choreographer of the Imperial Ballet, today known as the Mariinsky Ballet. Petipa created more than fifty ballets, including *The Pharaoh's Daughter* (1862), *Don Quixote* (1869), *La Bayadère* (1877), *The Sleeping Beauty* (1890) and *Raymonda* (1898). He also revived many works by other choreographers, and his revivals became the basis for most later productions, including *Giselle* and *Swan Lake* (with Lev Ivanov). He is considered one of the most influential ballet masters in history.

Roman politician and general. He helped transform the [[Roman Republic]] into the autocratic Roman Empire. A relative and supporter of [[Julius Caesar]], he served as one of Caesar's generals in the conquest of [[Gaul]] and in Caesar's civil war. After Caesar's assassination in 44 BC, Antony formed the Second Triumvirate with Octavian and Lepidus, and the triumvirs defeated Caesar's killers at Philippi in 42 BC. Antony had a love affair with [[Cleopatra]], ruler of [[Egypt]], who bore him three children, which strained his relations with Octavian. Octavian defeated Antony at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, and Antony and Cleopatra fled to Egypt, where, after a further defeat, they took their own lives. Octavian was then granted the title Augustus in 27 BC and became the first [[Roman emperor]].

American actor and voice actor. He became known for playing Luke Skywalker in the original *Star Wars* trilogy (1977–1983) and reprised the role in the sequel trilogy (2015–2019). Beginning in the 1990s he worked mainly as a voice actor, and his best-known voice role is the [[Joker (character)|Joker]] in *Batman: The Animated Series* (1992) and later DC Comics media. For that role he was nominated for two Annie Awards and won a BAFTA Game Award. His other animated roles include Fire Lord Ozai in *Avatar: The Last Airbender* (2005–2008). He also appeared on Broadway in the 1980s, in *Amadeus* (1983) and *The Nerd* (1987).

Latvian-born American abstract painter. He is best known for color field paintings of irregular, painterly rectangles of color, which he produced from 1949 to 1970. Rothko did not subscribe to any one school, though he is associated with the American [[Abstract expressionism|abstract expressionism]] movement. Born into a Jewish family in Daugavpils, Latvia, then part of the [[Russian Empire]], he emigrated to the United States with his family, arriving at [[Ellis Island]] in late 1913 and settling first in [[Portland, Oregon]]. He moved to New York City in 1923. He refunded the Seagram murals commission rather than see the paintings used as decor for wealthy diners, and the Harvard Mural series faded because of the pigment lithol red and sunlight exposure. He contributed 14 canvases to the Rothko Chapel in [[Houston]], Texas. His painting *No. 6 (Violet, Green and Red)* sold in 2014 for $186 million.

English actor, playwright and theater director. He was the first artistic director of Shakespeare's Globe in [[London]] from 1995 to 2005. On Broadway he has won three Tony Awards, two for Best Actor and one for Best Featured Actor. He won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for playing Rudolph Abel in *Bridge of Spies* (2015). He played [[Thomas Cromwell]] in the [[BBC]] mini-series *Wolf Hall* (2015) and completed the role in the 2024 sequel. In 2017 he was made a knight by Queen Elizabeth II.

American writer, humorist and essayist, known by the pen name Mark Twain. He wrote *The Adventures of Tom Sawyer* (1876) and its sequel, *Adventures of Huckleberry Finn* (1884), which is often called the "Great American Novel." He worked as a riverboat pilot on the [[Mississippi River]], an experience that provided material for *Life on the Mississippi* (1883). His first success came with the humorous story "The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County" (1865). Twain later opposed the [[Philippine–American War]] and American colonialism, and in 1905 he published a satirical pamphlet about Belgian atrocities in the [[Congo Free State]]. Investments in ventures such as the Paige Compositor, a typesetting machine, cost him most of his fortune, and he filed for bankruptcy. With help from [[Standard Oil]] executive Henry Huttleston Rogers, he later paid all his creditors in full.

American actor, producer and former rapper. He first came to fame in the 1990s as a member of the hip hop group Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch. He received critical praise for playing porn actor Dirk Diggler in *Boogie Nights* (1997). He was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for *The Departed* (2006) and for a Golden Globe for *The Fighter* (2010), in which he portrayed Micky Ward. He has starred in the *Transformers* films. As an executive producer he worked on five [[HBO]] series, including *Entourage*. He received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in 2010.

American businessman and programmer. He co-founded [[Facebook]] in February 2004 while a student at [[Harvard University]], and he is chairman and chief executive officer of its parent company, Meta Platforms. He took the company public in May 2012 and became the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2008. Under his leadership Meta acquired [[Instagram]] and [[WhatsApp]]. He and his wife established the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, pledging 99 percent of their Facebook shares to fund biomedical research and education. He has been the subject of lawsuits over the creation and ownership of Facebook and over user privacy.

In economics, any structure that allows buyers and sellers to exchange goods, services and information. Markets can be as small as a food market in a single building or as large as the worldwide [[Diamond|diamond]] trade. They differ by products, buyers, place of exchange, government regulation, taxes and size. Prices coordinate economic activity by conveying information among firms, households and individuals, and [[Supply and demand|supply and demand]] determine [[Price|prices]]. [[Microeconomics]] studies market structure and the efficiency of equilibrium; when equilibrium is not efficient, economists say a [[Market failure|market failure]] has occurred. In his 1937 article "The Nature of the Firm," Ronald Coase argued that the use of the price mechanism to convey information is the defining feature of the market.

Inefficient allocation of goods and services by a free market. In neoclassical economics, market failure is a situation in which the allocation is not Pareto efficient, often leading to a net loss of economic value. The term was first used by economists in 1958, although the concept has been traced to the Victorian writers [[John Stuart Mill]] and Henry Sidgwick. Market failures are associated with public goods, externalities, information asymmetries, failures of competition, principal–agent problems and unequal bargaining power. A [[Monopoly|monopoly]] can block mutually beneficial trade, and a natural monopoly arises where per-unit cost falls as output rises. Mainstream economists generally accept that governments or other organizations can sometimes improve market outcomes, as with building codes and [[Endangered species|endangered species]] laws. Critics argue that government interventions such as taxes, subsidies and regulations can also produce inefficiency, sometimes called government failure.

Location, physical or virtual, where people regularly gather to buy and sell goods. Such places are called souks, bazaars, mercados or palengkes in different regions. Some operate daily as permanent markets, while others meet weekly or on festival days. Open-air markets were known in ancient Babylonia, [[Phoenicia]], Greece and Egypt, and bazaars may have originated in Persia. From the 12th century, informal European markets gave way to formal, chartered markets, and medieval regulation of weights and measures strengthened consumer confidence. Middle Eastern markets are often covered to shelter traders from the sun. Many marketplaces are now accessible online through [[E-commerce|e-commerce]], and many historic markets are listed sites of architectural significance.

American YouTuber, filmmaker and actor, whose full name is Mark Edward Fischbach. He became known on [[YouTube]] for "Let's Play" videos of indie horror games, including the *Five Nights at Freddy's* series, after joining the platform in 2012. [[Forbes]] listed him as the third-highest-paid content creator on YouTube in 2022. As of August 7, 2026, his channel had over 38.8 million subscribers. He has won four Streamy Awards and a Golden Joystick Award. He directed, produced and starred in the horror film *Iron Lung* (2026), his theatrical debut.

[[Stochastic process|Stochastic process]] in which the probability of each event depends only on the state attained in the previous event. Named after the Russian mathematician Andrey Markov, Markov chains move between states at discrete time steps (discrete-time Markov chains) or continuously (continuous-time Markov chains). They serve as statistical models of real-world processes in fields such as [[Biology]], [[Economics]] and [[Physics]]. They provide the basis for Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, which sample from complex [[Probability distribution|probability distributions]] in [[Bayesian statistics]]. [[Google]]'s PageRank algorithm treats web links as transition probabilities, and hidden Markov models are used in speech recognition. Markov chains also appear in queueing theory in operations research.

Swedish video game programmer and designer, also known by the pseudonym Notch. He created [[Minecraft]], the best-selling video game in history, and founded Mojang Studios in 2009. In November 2014 Mojang was sold to [[Microsoft]] for a reported US$2.5 billion, which made him a billionaire. After the game's official retail release in 2011, he had stood down as lead designer and transferred creative authority to Jens Bergensten. Since 2016, several of his posts on Twitter about [[Feminism|feminism]], race and transgender rights have caused public controversy. Microsoft removed mentions of his name from Minecraft, except in the game's end credits.

American brand of cigarettes. Introduced in 1924 and first marketed to women, Marlboro was repositioned as a men's cigarette in the 1950s, after studies linked smoking to [[Lung cancer|lung cancer]]. The advertising campaign by the Leo Burnett agency featured the fictional cowboy known as the Marlboro Man. Philip Morris USA, a branch of Altria, manufactures the brand in the United States, and Philip Morris International does so in most other markets. Its largest plant is in [[Richmond, Virginia]]. The brand sponsored [[Formula One]] teams such as [[Ferrari]] and [[McLaren]]. Lawsuits have alleged deceptive marketing of its "light" cigarettes.

American actress and activist. Having been deaf since 18 months of age, she advocates for Deaf people in Hollywood and other industries. She made her acting debut in *Children of a Lesser God* (1986) and won the Academy Award for Best Actress, becoming the first Deaf performer to win an Academy Award and the youngest winner in that category. She played Joey Lucas on *The West Wing* (2000–2006) and voiced Stella in *Family Guy* (2012–2021). For *CODA* (2021) she shared a Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture.

German and American actress and singer whose career spanned nearly seven decades. Her performance as Lola Lola in Josef von Sternberg's *The Blue Angel* (1930) brought her international acclaim and a contract with [[Paramount Pictures]]. She starred in Hollywood films including *Morocco* (1930), her only Academy Award nomination, and *Shanghai Express* (1932). During [[World War II|World War II]] she was a high-profile entertainer in the United States, and she housed German and French exiles and advocated their American citizenship. Her postwar films included Billy Wilder's *A Foreign Affair* (1948) and [[Alfred Hitchcock]]'s *Stage Fright* (1950). In 1999 the American Film Institute named her the ninth greatest female screen legend of classic Hollywood cinema.

Family of fish, Istiophoridae, with between 9 and 11 species depending on the taxonomic authority. Marlins are elongated, predatory billfishes with a spear-like bill and a long, rigid dorsal fin. They are among the fastest marine swimmers, although exaggerated speeds are often claimed. The Atlantic blue marlin (*Makaira nigricans*) can reach 5 m in length and 820 kg in weight, and the black marlin (*Istiompax indica*) can exceed 5 m and 670 kg. Marlins are most closely related to the [[Swordfish]]. The Atlantic blue marlin and white marlin are endangered due to overfishing. [[Ernest Hemingway]]'s novel *The Old Man and the Sea* (1952) centers on a fisherman who hooks a marlin.

American actor noted for method acting. Born in [[Omaha, Nebraska]], he came under the influence of Stella Adler and the Stanislavski system in the 1940s, and he was among the first actors to bring that approach to mainstream audiences. On Broadway he played Stanley Kowalski in [[Tennessee Williams]]'s *A Streetcar Named Desire* (1947), a role he reprised in the 1951 film directed by [[Elia Kazan]]. He won two [[Academy Awards]] for Best Actor, for *On the Waterfront* (1954) and *The Godfather* (1972). He was also nominated for playing [[Mark Antony]] in *Julius Caesar* (1953) and for *Viva Zapata!* (1952). On television he won a Primetime Emmy for *Roots: The Next Generations* (1979), after which he took a nine-year break from acting. His final films included *The Island of Dr. Moreau* (1996) and *The Score* (2001).

Large ground squirrel of the genus *Marmota*. Marmots are the heaviest and largest members of the [[Squirrel|squirrel]] family. Their 15 species live in Asia, Europe and North America. Some inhabit mountain areas such as the [[Alps]] and the [[Rocky Mountains]], while others prefer rough grassland, such as the [[Eurasian Steppe]]. Marmots are active during the summer, when they are often found in groups, and [[Hibernation|hibernate]] underground in winter. They mainly eat grasses, berries, lichens, mosses, roots and flowers. Most species are highly social and use loud whistles to communicate, especially when alarmed. One researcher has argued that the "gold-digging ant" story reported by [[Herodotus]] was based on the golden Himalayan marmot.
